reviewItems.candidate: Bite the new shoots down at dusk and they stand above the old cut by morning. This place can answer feeding without pretending nothing was taken.

reviewItems.label: Page 2
reviewItems.candidate: Every shelter is occupied, and fresh tracks stop at the entrances before turning away. More creatures live here than one keeper could gather.

reviewItems.label: Page 3
reviewItems.candidate: Small grazers crowd the new growth. Larger tracks circle them, and scavengers follow what the hunt leaves behind. Feed one creature here and three others change their route.

reviewItems.label: Page 4
reviewItems.candidate: The same hollows are pressed flat each night while nearby ground goes untouched. Return often enough and absence becomes part of the pattern.

reviewItems.label: Page 5

reviewItems.label: Page 6
reviewItems.candidate: There is open ground enough to approach and cover near enough to refuse. I could work here without making nearness the only safe choice.

reviewItems.label: Page 7
reviewItems.candidate: The same calls begin at the same interval, and the same paths fill soon after. They can learn when I return; that does not mean they must come.

questions.title: What level should a named traveller join at?
questions.context: Named travellers currently join at level 1 even late in a long campaign. Active members then earn the same XP, so the gap never closes naturally. Encounter scaling correctly does not lower foe level to protect a recruit, which can leave a late arrival permanently fragile or unusable.
questions.recommendation: Have each named traveller join at the Binder's current level. Recruitment is already a major earned reward, and immediate parity lets the new person be played instead of parked. Their authored calling lean remains a bonus, while all level-earned combat points arrive unspent so the player chooses the build.

choices.title: Match Binder level
choices.detail: Join immediately usable at the Binder's current level, with level points banked and authored lean preserved.

choices.title: Two levels behind
choices.detail: Join slightly behind and add accelerated XP until the traveller reaches the Binder; more growth texture, but another persistent rule.

choices.title: Level 1 with catch-up
choices.detail: Preserve a full growth arc but grant strongly accelerated XP; late recruits may still need to sit out initially.

choices.title: Keep level 1
choices.detail: Accept that late named travellers begin far behind and require ordinary equal-share XP to advance.

questions.title: Who chooses what survives a failed expedition?
questions.context: The current failure rule floors each inventory stack separately, so splitting the same haul across item types can make far more of it disappear. That arithmetic will be corrected regardless of this choice. The remaining design question is whether the game automatically chooses which exact items fit the corrected retention budget or lets you change a deterministic suggested set before confirming.
questions.recommendation: Let the player choose within the fixed budget. Show a deterministic suggested set first, then allow swaps without changing how many items survive. Bulk world resources remain automatically apportioned, while pages, knowledge, recruited people and pre-departure property keep their existing protection.

choices.title: Let me choose
choices.detail: Show a suggested retained set, then let the player swap exact acquired items within the same fixed budget before confirming.

choices.title: Choose automatically
choices.detail: Use the corrected total-unit budget but select retained items deterministically from the expedition outcome, with no extra decision screen.

choices.title: Protect favourites first
choices.detail: Choose automatically but prioritize items the player marked as favourites; simpler at failure time, but attachment must be predicted before the expedition.

choices.title: Test arithmetic first
choices.detail: Ship only the corrected automatic arithmetic, then revisit player choice after failure recaps are trustworthy.

questions.title: How should named characters grow distinct stats?
questions.context: Every named traveller currently starts with the same all-equal stats. Level-up raises the two currently highest stats, but an equal starting line has no authored tie identity, so distinct callings can converge on the same Might/Finesse build. This is separate from combat-tree lean and from the level a traveller joins at.
questions.recommendation: Give each named person an authored primary and secondary growth stat, let the Binder choose a pair at new game, and freeze a generated pair for generated companions. Add one point to each per level. This keeps growth legible and identity-specific without asking the player to assign points across a large roster.

choices.title: Authored stat pair
choices.detail: Each named person grows two authored stats; Binder chooses and generated companions freeze a generated pair.

choices.title: Weighted rotation
choices.detail: Give each character a five-stat order or weighting and rotate two increases per level; more varied, but harder to read.

choices.title: Assign every point
choices.detail: Let the player choose both stat increases at every level; strongest control, with substantial roster upkeep.

choices.title: Keep highest two
choices.detail: Retain current growth and add only a deterministic tie-breaking rule.
